newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nemtsov says Russia wants lower interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Nemtsov says Russia wants lower interest rates.

text.p: Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Thursday the government would continue to put pressure on interest rates to fall to help the stagnating economy develop.
"I want to assure you that the federal government will continue to push down interest rates until money goes to the real sector," Nemtsov told a cabinet meeting.
"So all bankers starting with (the state-owned savings bank) Sberbank and all the commercial banks must understand this perfectly."
Russian factory managers complain they cannot raise extra capital through credits.

Russian banks are unwilling to lend to companies unless they have special relationships with them, typically owning a stake in the borrower. But bankers say the average level of credits even in these restricted circumstances is about 45 percent a year. Foreign banks rarely lend money to Russian companies directly.
Banks typically prefer to invest in government securities or other financial assets, rather than lend to industry.
Last month the central bank cut its refinancing rate to 24 percent from 36 percent and Treasury bill yields have fallen below 19 percent.
